text: A thousand years ago, parchment was precious. So when a text was no longer wanted, the scribes scraped it away, and wrote over it. But the old ink never quite left. A page like that is called a palimpsest.
Wikipedia is one, too. It has been rewritten eight hundred and sixty-two thousand times, and all we ever read is the top layer.
So we held it up to the light.
Now you can open any article, as it stood on any day. Lay two days side by side, and see every word that changed. Ask a question, and Gemini answers from the words of that day, right next to today's.
Follow a single claim back through every rewriting, to the hand that first wrote it. And see who changed what, down to the second.
Every edit is kept in MariaDB. Nothing we write is ever really gone. This is Palimpsest.
